# What lives in `.evie-kit/`

One rule decides where a file belongs: **everything at the root of this
directory is a SETTINGS file — a layer a human owns and edits.
Machine-generated state lives in `state/` and is never
edited by hand.**

## Root files — the settings layers (yours)

- `settings.ts`: the committed project settings base every agent
  session loads. Edit it, commit it.
- `settings.local.ts`: this machine's overrides (gitignored). Wins
  over the committed base where they disagree.
- `credentials.ts`: this machine's credentials — a
  root settings file like the two above (gitignored; written by
  `evie-kit setup`/`onboard`, never committed).
- `.gitignore`: managed by setup, append-only. It keeps the
  machine-local halves above (plus `runs/`, `handoffs/`,
  `conventions/*.local.md`, and migration ephemera) out of git.
  Upgrades re-add any missing rule without touching the rest.

## `state/`: machine-generated (never edit by hand)

- `state/copies.json`: which evie-kit produced each
  artifact setup copied into this repo. Committed;
  `evie-kit copies check` reads it to state how stale the copies are.
- `state/setup.json`: the setup wizard's recorded
  answers (never secrets). Committed; reruns read it to stay silent.

A `copies.json` or `setup.json` at the `.evie-kit/` root is the
pre-`state/` spot: readers still fall back to it, and the
next setup/upgrade run moves it here.

## `conventions/` (committed)

The project's naming and writing conventions — issue titles, commit
messages, branch names, labels, writing style. The `*.local.md`
halves are machine-local addenda and stay gitignored.

## `handoffs/` (gitignored)

Session handoffs: the structured pick-up notes a pausing agent session
writes for the next one. Machine-local by design.

## `runs/` (gitignored)

Machine-local run records. Nothing reads them across machines; safe to
delete.
